heard: A crashed space probe fell silent, yet spoke from Venus weeks later. On December 15, 1970, the Soviet Union reached the dark night side of Venus. Engineers built Venera 7 inside a thick titanium pressure shell to survive the extreme heat. During descent, the parachute failed, causing the heavy spacecraft to slam into the ground. Mission control assumed the probe died instantly after landing on its side. Weeks later, scientists found a faint 23-minute signal hidden beneath static on recorded tapes. The data confirmed a lead-melting surface temperature of 475 degrees Celsius. Hidden data revealed a crashed space probe talking from Venus.
